title: Choose onboarding by the first outcome
trigger: Every new account receives the same tour despite having different immediate jobs.
action: Ask one useful question such as 'What do you want to finish first?' and route to the shortest supported path for that outcome. Reuse the choice in examples and setup defaults while allowing it to be changed.
mechanism: A relevant path can make the product feel immediately applicable and reduce unrelated decisions.
guardrail: Do not collect role or goal data that does not change the experience; retain a route for uncertain users.
measure: First meaningful outcomes per new account; incorrect routing.

title: Defer setup unrelated to first value
trigger: New users must configure branding, invite a team, or complete a profile before doing useful work.
action: Map the minimum dependencies for the first valuable result and move unrelated setup behind a clear 'Do this later' option. Surface each deferred task when it becomes useful rather than hiding it permanently.
mechanism: A shorter path to a real result can reduce perceived effort and abandonment.
guardrail: Keep security, service-delivery, and required configuration prerequisites intact.
measure: Activated accounts; later configuration failures and setup debt.

title: Create editable starter work inside the account
trigger: A legitimate new account opens to a blank workspace and users do not know how to begin.
action: Offer an optional, clearly labeled starter project that the user can edit, duplicate, or remove inside their own workspace. Provide a direct transition to their real task rather than leaving them in a separate demonstration.
mechanism: Hands-on ownership can make the next useful action easier to imagine and attempt.
guardrail: Do not present sample work as the customer's achievement or create clutter that cannot be removed.
measure: First real projects completed; sample-only activity and cleanup complaints.

title: Preview imported data before committing it
trigger: Users hesitate to import because they cannot predict how their existing information will map into the product.
action: Show a small preview with detected columns, mapping choices, validation errors, and expected destination before starting the import. Let users correct the mapping without re-uploading a valid file.
mechanism: A reversible preview can reduce uncertainty about damaging or misplacing existing work.
guardrail: Protect private data, distinguish preview from a completed import, and verify the applied mapping matches the preview.
measure: Successful imports reaching value; incorrect records and rework.

title: Resume interrupted imports without starting over
trigger: Large imports or integrations fail midway and erase the user's setup effort.
action: Persist validated import progress where the system supports it, show completed and failed work separately, and allow a safe retry of only unresolved items. Explain whether the user may leave and return.
mechanism: Preserving invested effort can keep a technical interruption from ending product evaluation.
guardrail: Use idempotent processing and accurate progress; do not promise resumability the backend cannot provide.
measure: Imports completed after interruption; duplicates and abandoned accounts.

title: Connect only the source needed first
trigger: Onboarding asks for several integrations before the customer can evaluate one useful workflow.
action: Identify the smallest data source needed for the selected first task and request that connection at the point of use. Offer later connections when their additional value becomes relevant.
mechanism: A bounded setup request can reduce ambiguity and perceived commitment.
guardrail: Do not imply disconnected sources are integrated or fabricate results while permission is pending.
measure: Accounts reaching first value; connection failures and revoked access.

title: Make empty states start a real task
trigger: An empty dashboard says 'No items yet' but does not explain how to produce the promised outcome.
action: Replace the empty state with the specific next action and a suitable starting structure, such as 'Create your first invoice' with the required fields ready. Explain what will appear after completion.
mechanism: A concrete starting point reduces the gap between understanding the product and using it.
guardrail: Keep examples clearly marked and do not count opening a form as completed activation.
measure: Completed first tasks; empty-state exits and abandoned drafts.

title: Provide an expert route past onboarding
trigger: Experienced buyers must click through a beginner tour before performing a task they already understand.
action: Offer a visible direct-to-work path and keep guidance available on demand. Preserve necessary setup validation while allowing knowledgeable users to move through it without explanatory screens.
mechanism: Control over pace can reduce frustration for buyers who already have a clear intention.
guardrail: Do not skip mandatory security or data configuration; verify the direct path is fully usable.
measure: Time to first value by experience level; setup-related failures.

title: Count meaningful onboarding milestones only
trigger: The checklist rewards profile decoration or arbitrary clicks while users still cannot accomplish the core task.
action: Build the checklist from actual value milestones, such as connecting required data, producing a valid result, and using it. Mark completion from product state and allow optional tasks to be skipped.
mechanism: Visible progress toward a relevant goal can support continued effort.
guardrail: Do not fabricate completed steps, disguise paid commitments as setup, or equate checklist completion with retained value.
measure: Verified activation and paid conversion; checklist-only activity.

title: Guide the current first task in context
trigger: A long introductory tour describes features the user forgets before reaching the first task.
action: Show a short contextual instruction at the point of action, then reveal the next instruction after the actual state changes. Keep a route to dismiss or revisit guidance without blocking the task.
mechanism: Timely guidance can reduce working-memory demands and make the next action obvious.
guardrail: Verify anchors, keyboard access, and real completion signals; do not advance on clicks that failed.
measure: First-task completion; guidance dismissal and task errors.

title: Make first consequential actions reversible
trigger: New users avoid the core workflow because the first action appears capable of damaging data or contacting others.
action: Provide an actual preview, undo, draft, or sandbox route appropriate to the action. Explain which consequences are reversible before the user acts, and separate draft creation from publication or sending.
mechanism: A real reduction in risk can make experimentation with the product easier.
guardrail: Implement the promised reversal and retain explicit authorization for messages, publication, or destructive operations.
measure: First successful use; unwanted side effects and reversal failures.

title: Map workspace labels to familiar work
trigger: The product works, but default workflow labels and statuses do not match the customer's existing way of organizing the job.
action: Offer an editable mapping from the customer's terms to the supported workflow during the first real setup. Show how each familiar label corresponds to actual behavior, retaining the underlying rules and a way to restore defaults.
mechanism: Recognizable organization can reduce translation effort when moving an established process into a new tool.
guardrail: Do not imply renaming changes permissions or functionality; preserve integration mappings and explain unsupported process differences.
measure: Completed first workflows; misrouted work and configuration confusion.

title: Recognize a verified first useful result
trigger: The product celebrates after a button click even when the underlying job fails or produces nothing usable.
action: Show completion only after the actual result exists and meets the task's success conditions. Link directly to the result and explain what was accomplished in the customer's terms.
mechanism: Credible completion feedback can reinforce the connection between the product and useful progress.
guardrail: Keep pending, partial, failed, and completed states distinct; avoid celebrating sample data as real customer value.
measure: Verified first outcomes; false-success reports and early refunds.

title: Help users interpret their first output
trigger: A report or generated artifact appears, but new users cannot tell what matters or what to do next.
action: Highlight the relevant part of the actual result, explain its meaning in plain language, and suggest a supported next action. Let the user inspect the underlying data or assumptions where appropriate.
mechanism: Interpretation can turn a technically successful output into experienced value.
guardrail: Do not invent conclusions, hide uncertainty, or imply the result supports decisions beyond its reliability.
measure: Outputs used in a real task; misinterpretation and support contacts.

title: Invite collaborators after shareable value exists
trigger: Team products require invitations before the first user has anything useful to show.
action: Let the first user create a meaningful shareable artifact, then offer an invitation with a clear reason for the colleague to participate. Preview the intended role and message before any authorized send.
mechanism: A concrete shared object can make collaboration feel purposeful instead of like setup labor.
guardrail: Respect permissions and explicit send authorization; do not invite contacts automatically or expose private drafts.
measure: Collaborative activation; ignored invitations and access mistakes.

title: Offer useful work during unavoidable processing
trigger: A first-time workflow takes several minutes and leaves the user staring at a spinner.
action: Show truthful processing status and provide a relevant task that can safely be completed during the wait, such as reviewing an imported mapping or preparing the next input. Make returning to the result straightforward.
mechanism: Maintaining useful momentum may reduce the perceived cost of unavoidable waiting.
guardrail: Do not fabricate progress or distract from an action that requires attention; preserve status across navigation.
measure: Completed first outcomes; abandonment during processing.

title: Recover unsupported inputs with a concrete example
trigger: Users hit an unsupported file or format error during their first attempt and do not know how to repair it.
action: Explain the accepted structure, identify the incompatible part, and offer a downloadable example or supported conversion route. Preserve valid work while the input is corrected.
mechanism: A solvable correction can prevent an initial failure from defining the product experience.
guardrail: Do not promise automatic conversion that loses important data; validate the corrected input before processing.
measure: Successful second attempts; corrupted inputs and support effort.

title: Preserve the first artifact across interruptions
trigger: A new user creates useful work, leaves to obtain information, and returns to an empty editor.
action: Autosave permitted work or clearly support saving a draft, then restore the artifact and its state on return. Explain when work has actually been saved and where it can be found.
mechanism: Continuity protects the user's investment and makes returning feel worthwhile.
guardrail: Keep saving truthful, respect sensitive-data policies, and distinguish local drafts from durable server storage.
measure: Resumed tasks and paid activation; lost-work incidents.

title: Offer human help at a specific blockage
trigger: A complex setup step repeatedly fails and generic documentation does not address the user's situation.
action: Offer an optional help route with the failing step and non-sensitive diagnostic context already summarized. State the real availability and let the user choose whether to request assistance.
mechanism: A reachable expert can reduce uncertainty when the product cannot resolve a first-use barrier alone.
guardrail: Do not promise response times or included services without support capacity; send only with authorization.
measure: Assisted activations; support cost and unresolved expectations.

title: Let users plan their first real use
trigger: People register with an intention to return but have no concrete next task or suitable time selected.
action: Offer a small optional plan: choose the real task, required input, and intended time for the first session. Keep the plan editable and show it on return; offer reminders only through an authorized preference-based flow.
mechanism: A specific implementation intention may make a vague future goal easier to carry out.
guardrail: Do not manufacture urgency, create calendar events, or send reminders without the required user choice and authorization.
measure: First real use within the chosen window; unwanted reminders.
